nodes.name: POST /transcribe
nodes.notes:
YOUR TURN: Configure webhook authentication in the n8n UI.

WHAT: Receives audio files via HTTP POST (multipart/form-data).
WHY: Single entry point for all clients (Voxtype, Android, curl).
HOW: Listens at /webhook/transcribe. Clients POST with field 'file' containing audio (WAV, MP3, etc). Passes binary + headers downstream.
NEXT: Set Metadata captures timing and normalizes the audio binary.

GOTCHA: The external URL is /v1/audio/transcriptions (OpenAI standard). Caddy on VPS rewrites this to /webhook/transcribe before reaching n8n.

nodes.name: Set Metadata
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Captures pipeline start timestamp and normalizes audio binary.
WHY: Start timestamp is needed to calculate total pipeline latency. Binary must be renamed to 'file' for whisper.cpp compatibility.
HOW: Reads X-Client-Type header, finds uploaded audio binary, records file size in bytes, renames binary key to 'file'.
NEXT: Whisper STT receives the normalized 'file' binary.

GOTCHA: Use .bytes (not .fileSize) for audio size -- .fileSize returns a formatted string like '32.1 kB' which breaks SQL INSERTs.

nodes.name: FFmpeg Convert
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Converts any audio format to 16kHz mono WAV for Whisper compatibility.
WHY: Android clients send m4a/AAC which whisper.cpp cannot decode. Normalizes all input to Whisper's native format.
HOW: Writes binary to temp file, runs ffmpeg -ar 16000 -ac 1 -f wav, reads back, cleans up.
NEXT: Whisper STT receives guaranteed-compatible WAV audio.

LATENCY: ~20-50ms for typical 5-30s voice clips. Negligible vs pipeline total.

nodes.name: Whisper STT
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Sends audio to whisper.cpp server for transcription.
WHY: Whisper large-v3-turbo produces raw transcription. This is the first half of the STT pipeline.
HOW: HTTP POST to Desk (YOUR_HOST_IP:8083/v1/audio/transcriptions) with multipart form-data: audio file + response_format=verbose_json + bilingual initial_prompt for domain vocabulary.
NEXT: Process Whisper Response extracts text and detected language.

DESIGN: verbose_json gives us detected_language + word-level confidence. initial_prompt biases Whisper's token prediction toward tech vocabulary in both EN and FR. Timeout: 30s for long audio clips.

nodes.name: Process Whisper Response
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Extracts raw transcript and language, builds Qwen request.
WHY: Bridges Whisper output to Qwen input. The [LANGUAGE: X] tag prevents Qwen from translating between languages.
HOW: Reads verbose_json text + detected_language. Cleans newlines. Builds OpenAI chat completion request body with bilingual system prompt and prepends [LANGUAGE: English/French] to user message.
NEXT: Qwen Polish sends the prepared request to llama-server.

DESIGN: The 3B Qwen model needs an explicit language tag because the bilingual system prompt (mentioning French patterns) can confuse it into translating English input to French.

nodes.name: Qwen Polish
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Sends raw transcript to Qwen3 4B for accent/grammar correction.
WHY: Fixes Whisper transcription errors that acoustic model can't: accent patterns (ze/the), missing articles, French contractions, etc.
HOW: HTTP POST to Desk llama-server (YOUR_HOST_IP:8081/v1/chat/completions). Uses the _qwen_request body built by Process Whisper Response.
NEXT: Format Response extracts polished text for the client.

DESIGN: Qwen runs on EVERY request in Phase 1 -- no confidence-based skipping. Rationale: (1) Quality first. (2) Maximum training pairs. Skipping moves to Phase 4+ after LoRA fine-tuning.

nodes.name: Format Response
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Creates OpenAI-compatible transcription response JSON.
WHY: Standard format means all STT clients (Voxtype, Android apps) work out of the box without custom parsing.
HOW: Extracts polished text from Qwen response, detected language from Whisper, wraps in {text, task, language} format.
NEXT: Respond to Webhook sends this to the client.

GOTCHA: Cleans newlines from polished text (.replace) since verbose_json can include \n characters that break client display.

nodes.name: Respond to Webhook
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Returns the polished transcription to the HTTP client.
WHY: This is where the client gets their text back. Everything after this point is async and does NOT block the response.
HOW: Sends the Format Response JSON as HTTP 200 response.
NEXT: Async branch fires to save training data + latency metrics.

DESIGN: The async branch (training data + metrics) runs AFTER this node responds. The user gets polished text in ~300ms; DB writes happen in the background without adding latency.

nodes.name: Prepare Training Data
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Builds the SQL INSERT values for the training pairs table.
WHY: Every request produces a (raw, polished) transcript pair. These pairs will be used for LoRA fine-tuning of Whisper.
HOW: Collects raw_transcript, polished_transcript, timing data, model names, detected language. Sets needs_correction = true if raw != polished (meaning Qwen made changes).
NEXT: Save Training Pair writes to PostgreSQL.

nodes.name: Save Training Pair
nodes.notes:
YOUR TURN: Set up PostgreSQL credentials in n8n UI.

WHAT: INSERT into voice_training_pairs table.
WHY: Training data accumulates with daily use. Target: 50+ hours of approved pairs before first LoRA fine-tune (quarterly).
HOW: Uses n8n PostgreSQL node with 'Postgres account' credential. Connects to postgres-voice container on stmna_voice database.
NEXT: None (end of training data branch).

GOTCHA: Credential host must be 'postgres-voice' (container name), not the host IP. n8n reaches postgres via Podman external network.

nodes.name: Prepare Latency Data
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Builds the SQL INSERT values for the latency metrics table.
WHY: Per-request timing enables dashboards, regression detection, A/B model comparisons, and portfolio evidence.
HOW: Calculates whisper_total_ms, qwen_inference_ms, total_pipeline_ms from timestamps captured at each stage. Generates UUID request_id.
NEXT: Save Latency Metrics writes to PostgreSQL.

nodes.name: Save Latency Metrics
nodes.notes:
YOUR TURN: Uses same PostgreSQL credentials as Save Training Pair.

WHAT: INSERT into voice_latency_metrics table.
WHY: Latency data feeds Grafana dashboards and optimization decisions.
HOW: Same PostgreSQL connection as Save Training Pair.
NEXT: None (end of latency branch).

DESIGN: Both DB writes are async -- they run after Respond to Webhook has already sent the response to the client.

parameters.content:
## INGESTION

Webhook receives audio + Set Metadata captures timing.

Clients POST to /v1/audio/transcriptions (Caddy rewrites to /webhook/transcribe).
Supported formats: WAV, MP3, OGG, WebM.
Field name: 'file' (OpenAI standard).

## TRANSCRIPTION

Whisper STT transcribes audio on Desk (YOUR_HOST_IP:8083).

Model: large-v3-turbo Q5 (~3-4GB VRAM)
Output: verbose_json with detected_language
Bilingual initial_prompt biases toward EN/FR tech vocabulary.

## POST-PROCESSING

Qwen3 4B corrects accent/grammar errors.

Runs on EVERY request (Phase 1 -- no skipping).
Bilingual: detects EN/FR from Whisper, corrects in same language.
Model: Q4_K_M (~2.5GB) on Desk llama-server (YOUR_HOST_IP:8081).

## RESPONSE

Format + return polished text to client.

OpenAI-compatible JSON: {text, task, language}.
Client gets response in ~300ms (warm) before async logging starts.

## ASYNC LOGGING

Does NOT block the webhook response.

Saves to PostgreSQL (postgres-voice on Desk):
- voice_training_pairs: raw/polished pairs for LoRA fine-tuning
- voice_latency_metrics: per-request timing for dashboards

Audio archive to Nextcloud (AppsVM YOUR_HOST_IP):
- PLACEHOLDER -- configure Nextcloud WebDAV when ready
- Path: /STMNA_Voice/audio/YYYY-MM-DD/filename.wav

nodes.name: Prepare Audio Archive
nodes.notes:
PLACEHOLDER -- Not yet connected to Nextcloud.

WHAT: Prepares the upload path and metadata for Nextcloud WebDAV.
WHY: Audio files need to be archived for training data review and LoRA fine-tuning dataset export.
HOW: Will use HTTP Request node with WebDAV PUT to Nextcloud on AppsVM (YOUR_HOST_IP). Path: /STMNA_Voice/audio/YYYY-MM-DD/filename.wav
NEXT: Archive to Nextcloud (currently NoOp).

YOUR TURN: When ready, replace the NoOp with an HTTP Request node configured for Nextcloud WebDAV. You'll need:
- Nextcloud WebDAV URL: https://YOUR_NEXTCLOUD_DOMAIN/remote.php/dav/files/USER/
- Nextcloud app password for authentication
- Create the /STMNA_Voice/audio/ folder in Nextcloud first

nodes.name: Archive to Nextcloud
nodes.notes:
PLACEHOLDER -- NoOp (does nothing).

YOUR TURN: Replace this NoOp with an HTTP Request node when Nextcloud WebDAV is configured.

The HTTP Request should:
- Method: PUT
- URL: https://YOUR_NEXTCLOUD_DOMAIN/remote.php/dav/files/USER{{ $json._archive_path }}
- Auth: Basic auth with Nextcloud app password
- Body: Binary data (the original audio file)
- Send the audio from the webhook's binary data

nodes.name: Hallucination Filter
nodes.notes:
WHAT: Catches Whisper hallucination before Qwen polishing.
WHY: Short/noisy audio makes Whisper output phantom phrases (Thank you, Tschüss, Gracias) or repeat text. Cleaning here prevents Qwen from polishing garbage.
HOW: Three detection methods: (1) known phantom phrases, (2) segment no_speech_prob from verbose_json, (3) repetition detection.
NEXT: Process Whisper Response gets clean transcript.

When hallucination is detected, sets text to empty string. Downstream nodes handle empty transcript gracefully.
